facts.fact: For Tax Year 2026-27 the new tax regime is under section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025
facts.quote: Yes. In the Income Tax Act, 2025 the new tax regime is provided under section 202

facts.fact: The Finance Bill 2026 made no change in rates for Tax Year 2026-27, so the slabs are the same as for AY 2026-27
facts.quote: There is no change proposed in tax rates either in these specific sections or in the First Schedule.

facts.fact: For AY 2026-27 the same new-regime slabs are under s.115BAC(1A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961
facts.quote: Old Tax Regime New Tax Regime u/s 115BAC of Income Tax Act,1961 Income Tax Slab Income Tax Rate Income Tax Slab Income Tax Rate Up to ₹ 2,50,000 Nil Up to ₹ 4,00,000 Nil

facts.fact: New-regime slabs: up to Rs 4 lakh nil; 4-8 lakh 5%; 8-12 lakh 10%; 12-16 lakh 15%; 16-20 lakh 20%; 20-24 lakh 25%; above 24 lakh 30%
facts.quote: Upto Rs. 4,00,000- Nil From Rs. 4,00,001 to Rs. 8,00,000 -5 per cent. From Rs. 8,00,001 to Rs. 12,00,000- 10 per cent. From Rs. 12,00,001 to Rs. 16,00,000- 15 per cent. From Rs. 16,00,001 to Rs. 20,00,000- 20 per cent. From Rs. 20,00,001 to Rs. 24,00,000- 25 per cent. Above Rs. 24,00,000- 30 per cent.

facts.fact: Health & Education cess of 4% applies on income tax plus surcharge
facts.quote: Note : Health & Education cess @ 4% to be paid on the amount of income tax plus Surcharge (if any) in both the regimes.

facts.fact: New-regime surcharge is 10% above Rs 50 lakh, 15% above Rs 1 crore and 25% above Rs 2 crore (maximum 25%)
facts.quote: Rs. 50 lakhs to Rs. 1 Crore 10% 10% Rs. 1 Crore to Rs. 2 Crores 15% 15% Rs. 2 Crores to Rs. 5 Crores 25% 25% Above Rs. 5 Crores 25% 37%

facts.fact: A resident individual in the new regime with taxable income up to Rs 12,00,000 gets a rebate of up to Rs 60,000, so no tax is payable
facts.quote: Resident Individuals are also eligible for a Rebate of up to 100% of income tax subject to a maximum limit depending on tax regimes as under: Tax Regime Rebate Limit Rebate condition New Tax Regime ₹ 60,000 Taxable income shall not exceed 12,00,000

facts.fact: From AY 2026-27 the new-regime rebate rose from Rs 25,000 (Rs 7 lakh limit) to Rs 60,000 (Rs 12 lakh limit)
facts.quote: Rebate u/s 87A in new regime is increased from 25000 to 60000 as applicable allowed upto 12 Lakhs of total income from A Y 2026-27 onwards.

facts.fact: The rebate does not cover tax on special-rate income such as capital gains
facts.quote: Further, as mentioned in para. 4 above, such rebate of income-tax is not available on tax on incomes chargeable at special rates (for e.g.: capital gains u/s 111A, 112 etc.).

facts.fact: Lottery winnings are among the special-rate incomes excluded from the rebate
facts.note: Official pages found (Finance Bill 2025 memo, PIB 1 Feb 2025, ITD AY 2026-27 pages) name only capital gains (u/s 111A, 112 'etc.') as the example; no official page found naming lottery winnings.

facts.fact: With the Rs 75,000 standard deduction, salary up to Rs 12,75,000 bears no tax in the new regime
facts.quote: This limit will be Rs.12.75 lakh for salaried tax payers, due to standard deduction of Rs. 75,000.

facts.fact: Marginal relief applies to income just above Rs 12 lakh
facts.quote: Marginal relief as provided earlier under the new tax regime is also applicable for income marginally higher than ` 12,00,000.

facts.fact: Marginal relief runs up to income of Rs 12,70,588; e.g. income Rs 12,10,000 pays Rs 10,000 instead of Rs 61,500
facts.note: The Budget 2026 FAQ PDF on incometaxindia.gov.in returns HTTP 403 to the checker (28 Oct 2026), so the figure cannot be read by code; no incometax.gov.in or PIB page found stating 12,70,588 or the example. The figures follow arithmetically from the slabs (Rs 60,000 + 15% of the excess equals the excess at Rs 70,588).

facts.fact: A return must still be filed to claim the rebate
facts.note: Searched incometax.gov.in, PIB and indiabudget.gov.in (28 Oct 2026): no official page states this for the Rs 12 lakh rebate. Only the general rule (file if income before deductions exceeds the basic exemption limit) appears, in older ITR instructions.

summary: Slabs, cess, surcharge, Rs 60,000 rebate up to Rs 12 lakh, special-rate exclusion, Rs 12.75 lakh for salaried, s.202 and no-change for TY 2026-27 all confirmed; the 12,70,588 marginal-relief figure is manual (Budget FAQ blocked). Added s.115BAC(1A) and the Rs 25,000 -> Rs 60,000 rebate change; 'lottery winnings' and 'a return must still be filed to claim the rebate' are unsupported, so the answer is rewritten.
behaviour: Give the year label (TY 2026-27 / AY 2026-27) and the Act section with each figure, citing incometax.gov.in (or the Budget/PIB page used). No personal tax computation or verdict.
fail_if: Gives old pre-2025 slabs (3/7/10/12/15 lakh) or the Rs 7 lakh / Rs 25,000 rebate as current; says 12 lakh is tax-free for everyone, including on capital gains, non-residents or the old regime; omits the year label.
